title: Form probes: do creeper, weeping or prostrate read as a new KIND of plant?
question: Ignoring size for a moment -- which of these, if any, reads as a different kind of plant from the tree, rather than a tree that grew differently?
context_md:
WP-C. Three probes against the four-axes bar in `plant-evolution-design.md` §4a. Same scene, same seed, same 3 noon frames (10,800 / 18,000 / 25,200), `tree` re-rendered in the same batch as the control.

**What I already think, so you can disagree with it:** creeper reads as a new class to me; prostrate reads as the same thing creeper is; weeping reads as a shaggier, lower tree rather than a new class. That is 1 against a bar of 2, so on my reading this round does *not* validate the "envelope is wide" claim -- which is the claim you already pushed back on.

**What I want you to ignore:** absolute plant size. Creeper and prostrate are deliberately tiny (5-8 row turgor budget). The question is whether they are a different *kind of object*, not whether they are smaller.

**What I have not measured:** no cell census. The size-class claim is read off these sheets, which is exactly the quantity a picture cannot give. Say the word and I will run one.

`sites` below is scheduled growth sites at frame 25,200 -- 0 means the plant has finished growing and gone quiet.
